title: A Ghost for the Contact
premise: Casper Oyelaran, a freelance interpreter for a fragile peace delegation in the border city of Vellmark, has spent years translating other people's truths while hiding his own: he was once the man who leaked a delegation's security schedule, and people died. When his handler, Ilse Brandt, is found dead — yet sends him a calendar invitation for a meeting she scheduled before dying — Casper follows it into a conspiracy inside the delegation itself. A staged 'accident' is set to kill both delegations' leaders and bury the peace process along with his old crime. To stop it, Casper must expose himself as the leak from years ago, trading his polished lie for justice no court will deliver. In the end he saves the summit, surrenders to an inquiry on his own terms, and finally belongs to something true.
about_author: Hazel Blackwood is a former conference interpreter turned novelist who writes thrillers about people caught between languages, loyalties, and lies. She lives between two countries and insists that every story worth telling begins with someone saying one thing and meaning another.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Casper Oyelaran's POV. During a tense pre-summit session in Vellmark, Casper softens a hostile phrase to keep talks alive while privately rehearsing his exit plan: go-bag by the door, false passport, a lie about his past worn smooth. His handler Ilse Brandt warns him that someone inside the delegation is asking about interpreters' histories. Emotional beat: uneasy competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Invitation from the Dead
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. News breaks that Ilse drowned in her hotel bath — ruled accidental. That night his phone buzzes: a meeting invitation from Ilse's account, tomorrow, 06:00, Room 114, sent hours after her death. He goes despite every instinct. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion; the first crack in his controlled world.

chapters.title: Room 114
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, brief interlude in security chief Dana Kovac's POV. The room holds Ilse's hidden notes: a ciphered page suggesting the summit 'accident' is scheduled, and a note naming Casper as the only person she trusted. Kovac, investigating Ilse's death, notices Casper leaving and begins pulling his file. Emotional beat: chosen danger; being seen.

chapters.title: What Interpreters Hear
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Working a closed-door session, Casper catches a delegate's slip in a language the principals don't share — a reference to 'the generator floor' and a date. He realizes the attack will be disguised as an infrastructure failure during the joint signing. Emotional beat: the vertigo of knowledge no one asked him to have.

chapters.title: The Leak He Was
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Casper's POV. Years ago, Casper leaked a delegation's movement schedule to settle a debt; three aides died. He rebuilt himself as clean-handed Hazel-blackwood-honest Casper. Now Kovac confronts him with fragments of that old file, forcing him to choose between silence and confession. Emotional beat: shame resurfacing; identity under interrogation.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Casper and Kovac. Uneasy alliance forms — she needs his linguistic access, he needs her clearance. They trace Ilse's cipher to a procurement shell company buying the venue's maintenance contract. But their evidence is thin, and the delegation's own security chief appears to be shielding someone. Emotional beat: fragile trust between two liars.

chapters.title: Countdown in Three Languages
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Forty-eight hours out. Casper volunteers to interpret the technical walkthrough on the generator floor, mapping exits, timers, and the conspirators' faces. He identifies the inside man: Deputy Head of Mission Aris Vey, whose idealism has curdled into a belief that the peace must fail spectacularly. Emotional beat: cold clarity; fear converted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Trap They Set for Him
chapters.summary: Kovac's POV, then Casper's. Their plan to lure Vey into a recorded confession collapses — Vey was expecting them, and Kovac is suspended on fabricated misconduct charges. Casper is now alone, discredited in advance, with the attack hours away. Emotional beat: betrayal, isolation, the temptation to simply run with the go-bag.

chapters.title: Accident Pending
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Signing day. Casper uses his interpreter's booth — the one place he can speak as anyone — to broadcast a warning through the delegation's own headset channel, then physically intervenes on the generator floor as the sabotage triggers early. A brutal close-quarters struggle; he stops the cascade but is injured and identified. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, coda weeks later. Vey is arrested; the summit resumes without its accident. Casper, healed but changed, voluntarily testifies about both conspiracies — including his own old leak — accepting whatever judgment follows. He unpacks the go-bag at last, keeping only Ilse's note. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth; justice outside the law, answered inside it.
